complexity.explanation: Insertion sort builds the final sorted array one element at a time. It has linear time complexity in the best case (already sorted array) and quadratic in the worst case (reverse sorted).

description.brief: A simple sorting algorithm that builds the final sorted array one element at a time by repeatedly inserting each element into its correct position among the previously sorted elements.
detailed: • Best case:    O(n)   - when array is already sorted
• Worst case:   O(n²)  - reverse sorted data
• Online algorithm - can sort as elements arrive
• Stable - maintains relative order of equal elements
• Adaptive - performs better on partially sorted data
• Comparisons: n(n-1)/2 ≈ O(n²) in worst case
• Assignments: Up to n(n-1)/2 in worst case
1. Assume first element is already sorted
3. Compare key with elements in sorted portion
4. Shift larger elements to the right
6. Repeat until all elements are sorted
optimizations: Binary insertion sort (binary search for insertion position)
Hybrid with merge sort for larger datasets
Using sentinel to avoid bounds checking
use_cases: Online sorting where elements arrive one by one
disadvantages: Quadratic time complexity for large datasets
Not suitable for reverse sorted data
Requires shifting many elements in worst case
Inefficient compared to O(n log n) algorithms for large n
